  <action>
Create `src/app/integration/README.md`. This is the artifact that makes the new directory exist in git and gives the two integration specs a stated convention instead of an unexplained departure from co-location.

Content it must cover:
- What belongs here: a spec that exercises two or more collaborating units through their real wiring, where no single source file is its owner. Name the counter-case explicitly — a spec that tests one source file belongs beside that file, per the repo's existing convention.
- Naming: `<flow-name>.integration.spec.ts`, kebab-case, named after the user-facing flow rather than after any participating class. The two initial members are `share-link-import.integration.spec.ts` and `upload-attach-use.integration.spec.ts`.
- Mocking posture: stub only what crosses a process or network boundary. For the share-link flow that is global `fetch` and nothing else; for the upload flow that is image processing and `FileReader`, with persistence left real. State the reasoning — the value of a spec in this directory is that the wiring between units is real, so every additional spy erodes the reason the file is here rather than co-located.
- Cleanup obligation: any spec here that writes to real persistence must restore it in `afterEach`, because IndexedDB survives across the whole Karma run and would otherwise leak into later spec files.
- Build config: no change needed; `tsconfig.spec.json` already includes `src/**/*.spec.ts`.
- A pointer to `.planning/phases/05-test-coverage-hardening/05-CONTEXT.md` D-09 as the decision of record.

Also note in the README that `src/app/testing/` is the sibling home for shared fixtures and harnesses that are imported by specs but are not themselves specs — that split is what keeps this directory holding only runnable flows.

Do not create placeholder or stub `.spec.ts` files here. 05-10 and 05-11 create the real ones; an empty or `xit`-only placeholder would register as a passing spec file and misreport coverage.
  </action>
